newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian gas firm's deputy chief missing.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian gas firm's deputy chief missing.

text.p: Bulgaria's interior ministry said on Thursday it was searching for the deputy executive director of Bulgaria's gas state monopoly Bulgargas who had been missing since midnight.
Penko Dimitrov went to Bulgargas headquarters in Sofia at 1015 GMT on Wednesday telling the guards he needed to pick up medicine from his office, a ministry statement said.

They spotted a strange vehicle parked outside and had offered to accompany Dimitrov on his way out. He declined the offer and went to the car, which sped away. Dimitrov has not been seen since, it said.
Bulgargas officials were not available for comment.
The ministry said recently it had to take special steps to protect Bulgargas executive director Vassil Filipov, who had been threatened.

Last month Filipov protested against the high prices of natural gas supplies paid to Topenergy, a Bulgarian-Russian joint gas stock company which is half-owned by Russia's Gazprom. He said he would seek better offers from other foreign firms.

On Tuesday, an attempt was made to assassinate Ilia Pavlov, head of Bulgaria's biggest powerful business conglomerate, Multigroup, but he was not in either of the cars travelling on a mountain road outside Sofia when the incident occurred.
Crime has flourished in the Balkan country since the end of one-party rule in 1989.
